$comment: Settings for scripts/compile-sv.mjs. inherit: a lesson bench that builds on another lesson's bench takes these files from it. known: units that fail for a recorded reason (kind verilator-limitation, content-bug or harness); each content-bug entry is debt to fix.

T1_Foundational/F2A_Core_Data_Types/inde.reason: Verilator 5.052 rejects `4'b1001 inside {a4}` (lesson lines 700 and 702) with 'RHS of ==? or !=? is fourstate but not a constant'. IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.13 allows any expression as a set member and says x or z bits in a set value are do-not-care, as with wildcard equality (11.4.6), so the construct is legal.

T1_Foundational/F2A_Core_Data_Types/oper.reason: Verilator 5.052 does not support a non-constant 4-state right operand of ==? (4'b1010 ==? nib), or of inside, which compares each member with ==? ({nib, 4'b0000}). Both are legal: IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.6 puts no constant restriction on either operand of ==? and treats x/z in the right operand as wildcards, and 11.4.13 (Syntax 11-3) allows any expression as a set member and compares integral members with ==?.

T1_Foundational/F2C_Procedural_Code_and_.reason: Legal code: the Kata B worked solution's `task automatic xfer(..., output bit timed_out)` writes its output argument with a blocking assignment after `#40` inside a nested fork. IEEE 1800-2023 §13.3 says an output is copied out when the task ends, and its Example 2 (task light) writes an output after an event control. §13.3.2 forbids only nonblocking or procedural continuous assignments to automatic task variables, their use in intra-assignment event controls of NBAs, and tracing them with $monitor/$dumpvars. §9.3.2 restricts only ref arguments in join_any/join_none. Verilator 5.052 rejects the write and cites 'IEEE 1800-2023 13.2.2', a subclause that does not exist (§13.2 has no subclauses).

T1_Foundational/F3A_Simulation_Semantics.reason: Verilator 5.052 rejects `$printtimescale($root);` (lesson line 563) because its parser accepts `$root` only as the start of a hierarchical name (`$root.x`). IEEE 1800-2023 §20.4.2 makes it legal: Syntax 20-4 takes a hierarchical_identifier, the clause says that with the argument `$root` the task displays the simulation time unit (§3.14.3), and the standard's own example calls `$printtimescale($root);`.

T1_Foundational/F3B_Scheduling_Regions/i.reason: Verilator 5.052 rejects the worked example's `program tb_prog; ... endprogram` declared inside `module tb_top` (lesson line 362-369), reporting 'Unsupported: program decls within module decls'. This is legal: IEEE 1800-2023 Annex A.1.4 lists program_declaration as a non_port_module_item, and §24.3 says program blocks can be nested within modules or interfaces, and that a nested program with no ports is implicitly instantiated once.

T1_Foundational/F4C_Clocking_Blocks/inde.reason: Verilator 5.052 reports 'Unsupported: program decls within module decls' for the port-less program tb_prog nested in module tb_top. IEEE 1800-2023 §24.3 allows it: program blocks can be nested within modules or interfaces, and nested programs with no ports are implicitly instantiated once.

Verilator 5.052 crashes (V3AssertPre.cpp:453 'Non-constant cycle delay') on the procedural '##(n);' in interface task wait_cycles. IEEE 1800-2023 §14.11 allows it: the syntax includes '## ( expression )', the cycle delay can be any expression that evaluates to a non-negative integer (example '##(j + 1);'), and cb is the interface's default clocking (§14.12).

T2_Intermediate/I-SV-2B_Advanced_Constra.reason: Verilator 5.052 rejects 'it.randomize(null)' (lesson line 317) on a class with rand dynamic-array members ('Unsupported: randomize(null) on class with rand container or class member'). IEEE 1800-2023 §18.11.1 (Inline constraint checker) explicitly defines randomize() with the special argument null as a checker that treats every member as a state variable and returns 1 only if all constraints hold. With that one call commented out, the rest of frame_pkg compiles with 0 errors.

tb_top borrows frame_pkg (block #1, lesson line 232), so it hits the same Verilator 5.052 'Unsupported: randomize(null) on class with rand container or class member' error, at lesson line 317. The call is legal under IEEE 1800-2023 §18.11.1 (Inline constraint checker). With the call removed, tb_top and frame_pkg compile together with 0 errors.

Verilator 5.052 reports 'Unsupported: randomize(null) on class with rand container or class member' for f.randomize(null) (lesson line 454) on a class with a rand dynamic array. IEEE 1800-2023 18.11.1 (Inline constraint checker) makes this legal: randomize() accepts the special argument null, so every class member is a state variable and the call only checks the active constraints. A lint probe with only that call worked around found no other errors.

T2_Intermediate/I-SV-3A_Functional_Cover.reason: Verilator 5.052 does not support calling coverage methods on a coverpoint by member access (cov.cp_kind.get_inst_coverage(), cov.cp_len.get_inst_coverage()). This is legal: IEEE 1800-2023 19.8, Table 19-5, says get_inst_coverage() can be called on a coverpoint through the . operator. With those two calls stubbed, the rest of the unit lints with no errors.

Verilator 5.052 does not support calling a predefined coverage method on a coverpoint (cov.cp_addr.get_inst_coverage(covered, total)). IEEE 1800-2023 19.8 (Table 19-5) makes get_inst_coverage() and get_inst_coverage(ref int, ref int) callable on a covergroup, a coverpoint or a cross, and its own example calls cv1.x.get_inst_coverage(covered,total).

Verilator 5.052 does not support member access to a coverpoint or cross of an embedded covergroup (cov.cg.addr_x_op.get_inst_coverage(covered, total), cov.cg.cp_addr.get_inst_coverage()). IEEE 1800-2023 19.8 (Table 19-5) allows get_inst_coverage() on coverpoints and crosses through the . operator.

Two Verilator 5.052 limitations. It does not support member access to coverpoints and crosses (cov.cg.cp_kind.get_inst_coverage(c, t)), which IEEE 1800-2023 19.8 (Table 19-5) allows. Past that, it crashes with an internal error ('AstNode is not of expected type ... ENUMITEMREF') on a transition bin with enum constants (bins ctrl_then_data = (CTRL => DATA), lesson line 858). That bin is legal under 19.5.2 (Syntax 19-3), where trans_item is a covergroup_range_list of integral values.

T2_Intermediate/I-SV-3B_Advanced_Functio.reason: Verilator 5.052 cannot access a covergroup's coverpoints and crosses as members, so it rejects cg.cp_op.get_inst_coverage(c, t) and cov[0].cg.x_op_a.get_coverage(). IEEE 1800-2023 19.8 (Table 19-5) makes get_coverage() and get_inst_coverage(ref int, ref int) callable on a coverpoint or cross through the instance '.' operator. Once those calls are worked around, the rest of the unit lints with no errors.

Verilator 5.052 rejects the system function $get_coverage() (IEEE 1800-2023 §19.9 defines it, returning the overall coverage of all covergroup types as a real 0 to 100). Past that, it also rejects coverage methods called on a coverpoint or cross, such as c.cg.cp_op.get_inst_coverage(covered, total) and lane0.cg.cp_op.get_coverage(covered, total) ('Member not found in covergroup'), which Table 19-5 and the §19.8 example cv1.x.get_inst_coverage(covered,total) make legal.

Verilator 5.052 cannot resolve coverpoint and cross members of a covergroup instance. That covers method calls like cov.cg.x_op_a.get_inst_coverage(covered, total) and cov.cg.cp_op.get_inst_coverage(...), and reading an instance option like cov.cg.cp_op.option.comment. All of it is legal: IEEE 1800-2023 19.8 Table 19-5 allows get_coverage()/get_inst_coverage(ref int, ref int) on a coverpoint and on a cross, and 19.7 shows per-item instance options accessed through the instance (g1.a.option.weight = 3).

Verilator 5.052 does not support accessing members of a coverpoint or cross through the covergroup instance: cg.cp_op.get_inst_coverage(c, t) and cg.cp_op.option.comment fail with "Member 'cp_op' not found in covergroup". The code is legal under IEEE 1800-2023 19.8 (Table 19-5 lists get_inst_coverage(ref int, ref int) as callable on a coverpoint or cross; the clause's example calls cv1.x.get_inst_coverage(covered,total)) and 19.10 (option is an implicitly declared struct member of every coverpoint and cross).

T2_Intermediate/I-SV-4B_Advanced_Tempora.reason: Verilator 5.052 has two gaps here, both in p_in_order_data. First, it crashes with 'Internal: Unexpected Call' on show_pair(...) attached as a sequence_match_item to (out_vld && out_rdy && out_cnt == tkt)[->1], which IEEE 1800-2023 16.11 allows (it lets tasks, void functions and system tasks attach to a nonempty-matching sequence and allows local variables as by-value arguments). Second, with the call removed, it reports 'Unsupported: property local variable used across composite sequence operator in consequent' for tkt/exp_data, assigned in the antecedent and read after the goto repetition, which 16.10 allows (its own example is a ##1 (!a, x = data_in) |=> !b[*0:$] ##1 b && (data_out == x)).

Verilator 5.052 does not parse a clocking event inside a property or sequence expression. It rejects `src_pulse |=> @(posedge dst_clk) ##[0:3] dst_pulse` (assert) and `src_pulse ##1 @(posedge dst_clk) ##[0:3] dst_pulse` (cover) with "unexpected '@'", and in a named sequence it reports "Unsupported: clocking event inside sequence expression". IEEE 1800-2023 makes both legal: §16.13.2 defines multiclocked `|=>` (wait for the nearest strictly later tick of the consequent clock), §16.13.1 defines multiclocked sequences joined by `##1`, and §16.7 gives `sequence_expr ::= clocking_event sequence_expr`.

T2_Intermediate/I-SV-4C_Checkers/index#5.reason: Verilator 5.052 rejects three legal bind forms: a package-scoped checker name (`bind fifo fifo_chk_pkg::fifo_chk u_chk (...)`), a hierarchical instance list (`bind fifo : tb_top.u_rx, tb_top.u_tx ...`) and a hierarchical single-instance target (`bind tb_top.u_dbg fifo_logger u_log (...)`). All three are legal under IEEE 1800-2023 §23.11 Syntax 23-9 (bind_target_instance ::= hierarchical_identifier constant_bit_select; bind_instantiation includes checker_instantiation) and §17.3 Syntax 17-2 (ps_checker_identifier ::= [package_scope] checker_identifier). The unit is complete: fifo, fifo_chk_pkg, fifo_logger and tb_top with u_rx, u_tx and u_dbg are all compile blocks in the lesson.

T2_Intermediate/I-SV-5_Synchronization_a.reason: Verilator 5.052 rejects assigning one event variable to another in a module ("Assignment to and from event in statically scheduled context"). IEEE 1800-2023 §6.17 lets an event variable be assigned another event variable, and §15.5.5 and §15.5.5.1 (merging events) show module-level assignments like `E2 = E1;`; this example is adapted from the one in §15.5.5.1.

In the kata solution, the automatic task get_with_timeout makes a blocking write to its output formal (`ok = 1'b1;`, lesson line 960) after `gen2drv.get(t)` blocks, inside a nested fork. This is legal in IEEE 1800-2023: §13.3 copies outputs back when the task completes, and its traffic_lights example writes an output after `@(posedge clock)`. §13.3.2 and §6.21 forbid only nonblocking, continuous and procedural continuous writes to automatic variables, plus $monitor/$dumpvars tracing, and §6.21 makes a fork-join block's lifetime cover all its spawned processes. The §9.3.2 fork-join_any rule covers only ref formals. Verilator's cited clause '13.2.2' does not exist (13.2 Overview has no subclauses).

T2_Intermediate/I-SV-6_Compiler_Directiv.reason: Kata 1's worked solution uses module `link` from the kata's Given block (lesson line 1031). Spine §5.2 item 1 allows that, and the code is legal: IEEE 1800-2023 §23.11 resolves the bind's actuals `.clk, .rst_n, .valid(lane_valid), .data(lane_data)` and `#(.N(LANES))` from the viewpoint of the target link instance. Compiled after the Given block, it has 0 errors. Run alone, Verilator 5.052 stops at the bind's 'Can't find definition of variable: clk/rst_n' before it reports MODMISSING for link, so the harness never borrows the Given block. Known entry: id ...index#4, kind harness. The old #9 id no longer exists.

T2_Intermediate/I-SV-7_DPI_and_Foreign_L.reason: The exported task sv_send_word waits on `@(cb);` (lesson line 839). It is called from `import "DPI-C" context task c_send_words`, which is declared in the same module tb_top. This is legal in IEEE 1800-2023. §35.8 says exported tasks follow the §35.7 rules (an export in the defining module scope) and that a context imported task may call an exported task. Its int return value reports the disable state (§35.9). §35.5.1.5 and the NOTE in §35.5.1.1 say an exported task may run a delay, event control or wait, which suspends the calling thread. Verilator 5.052 rejects any timing control inside a DPI-exported task, and its generated header even declares the export as `void sv_send_word(unsigned int)`, not the `int` result that §35.8 requires.

T3_Advanced/B-AHB-2_AHB_Pitfalls_and_Dea.reason: Verilator 5.052 does not support the gated form $past(HADDR[31:10], 1, HREADY && HTRANS inside {NONSEQ, SEQ}) in p_incr_no_1kb_cross (lesson line 812). IEEE 1800-2023 §16.9.3 makes it legal: $past(expression1 [, number_of_ticks [, expression2 [, clocking_event]]]), where expression2 gates the clocking event. The probe found no other error.

T3_Advanced/B-AHB-3_AHB_Verification/ind.reason: Verilator 5.052: Unsupported: $past expr2 and/or clock arguments. The checker's $past(expr, 1, beat_accepted) in a_seq_ctrl_matches, a_seq_addr_increments and a_incr_no_1kb_cross (lesson lines 990, 996, 1004) is legal: IEEE 1800-2023 16.9.3 defines expression2 as a gating expression for the clocking event.
